pr_title: Remove resize index settings once shards are started
pr_body:
This commit removes the specific index settings used to resize indices during clone/split/shrink.

Settings are removed once all primary shards are started. This is implemented in a new `RoutingChangesObserver` in order to not add more complexity to the existing `IndexMetadataUpdater`.

Closes #90127

Edit:  Sadly ILM relies on the `INDEX_RESIZE_SOURCE_NAME_KEY` setting to identify an index that has been shrunk. I suppose this information was not added to ILM lifecycle execution state to keep it minimal but it now makes this change harder to implement. I've updated the code to not remove this index settings for ILM managed indices but I would prefer ILM to maintain its own metadata in its execution state, specially when an information is required after the ILM action is done.

issue_context.title: Remove resize left-over at shard started
issue_context.body:
When a resize (shrink/clone/split) occurs, the new index gets `index.resize.source.uuid` and `index.resize.source.name` set in order to indicate the source of the operation. For shrink we also set `index.routing.allocation.initial_recovery.<something>` to force the location of the shrunk shards to go on the node holding the source shards.

Today this is left as is once the shard is started. But at this time, the shards are now decoupled and these indications are no longer used. This is enforced in allocation deciders by ensuring that we only check these for unassigned shards with recovery source `LOCAL_SHARDS`. Notice that the resize source index is often deleted afterwards, making the reference to the source index sort of dangling.

I propose to remove this at shard started (of the last shard), such that it is clear that these are no longer in use.

Relates #89768
